content:
An online store in India succeeds or fails on details that have little to do with design: whether UPI payments go through smoothly, whether COD orders turn into returns, whether the GST invoice is correct, and whether the buyer can see that you deliver to their pincode. We build e-commerce websites from our office on Sohna Road for Gurugram D2C brands, retailers, distributors and manufacturers moving into online ordering. This page covers the decisions you will face, how the build works and what can go wrong.

Start with how your orders actually work

Before we talk about platforms or design, we ask questions about your operations. The answers shape the whole store:

  • Who is buying? Retail customers (B2C), businesses ordering in bulk (B2B), or both. B2B buyers usually need GSTIN on invoices, quantity pricing and sometimes credit terms.
  • How many products and variants? Twenty kurtas in five sizes is a very different catalogue from 3,000 auto parts with fitment data.
  • Where is stock held? One warehouse, a few stores, or an existing billing or ERP system that needs to stay in sync.
  • How much COD will you accept? Cash on delivery lifts conversions but brings returns-to-origin, so we plan rules around it.
  • Who packs and ships? Your own team with a courier aggregator, or a fulfilment partner.

Platforms we build on

  • WooCommerce
  • Shopify
  • Custom PHP / Laravel

WooCommerce runs on WordPress and suits stores that want full control, content-heavy product pages or unusual pricing rules, with no platform subscription. You manage hosting, updates and security, or pay someone to. Shopify suits brands that want a managed platform and fast setup, and are comfortable with monthly subscription and app costs. A custom build makes sense only for requirements the platforms handle badly, such as a dealer portal with customer-specific price lists. We recommend the platform after the operations questions above, not before.

Payments, GST and cash on delivery

This is where Indian stores lose most orders, so we spend real time on it:

  • Payment gateway set-up with Razorpay, PayU or Cashfree, covering UPI, cards, net banking and wallets. Gateways run their own KYC, so we prepare the policy pages they look for.
  • GST-ready invoices with your GSTIN, HSN codes, correct CGST/SGST or IGST depending on the delivery state, and an optional GSTIN field at checkout for business buyers.
  • COD rules: turn it off above a set order value or for certain pincodes, add a COD fee if you choose, and confirm COD orders by OTP or WhatsApp before dispatch to cut fake orders.
  • Failed payment recovery: clear retry options and reminder messages when a UPI payment times out.
  • Refunds processed from the admin panel through the gateway, so your team is not doing bank transfers by hand.

Shipping, pincodes and returns

We connect the store to a shipping aggregator such as Shiprocket, or directly to a courier like Delhivery, so that shipping labels and AWB numbers are created from the order screen. Buyers can check delivery availability and an estimated date by pincode on the product page, and receive tracking updates by email, SMS or WhatsApp. We also set up return and exchange requests so they reach your team as structured tickets rather than scattered messages.

The build, stage by stage

A store with a clean product sheet of up to a few hundred products typically takes 6 to 10 weeks. Larger catalogues, ERP sync or B2B features add time.

  1. Operations workshop (week 1): the questions above, plus shipping zones, taxes and policies.
  2. Design (weeks 2 to 3): home, category, product, cart and checkout pages designed mobile-first, because most buyers will shop on a phone.
  3. Development and integrations (weeks 3 to 7): store set-up, gateway, shipping, invoices, WhatsApp and email notifications.
  4. Catalogue import (overlaps with development): products loaded from your spreadsheet, images optimised, categories and filters set.
  5. Test orders and launch (final 1 to 2 weeks): real transactions on every payment method, then go-live and close monitoring of the first orders.

What you need to prepare

  • A product spreadsheet: name, SKU, price, MRP, variants, weight, dimensions, HSN code and a short description for each item.
  • Product photos on a plain background, with consistent size and lighting across the range.
  • Business PAN, GST registration and a current account for gateway KYC.
  • Your shipping, returns, refund and cancellation policies, which we can help you write in plain language.
  • Decisions on COD limits, free-shipping thresholds and discount rules.

How we check the store before launch

  • Real test orders on UPI, cards, net banking and COD, including a failed payment and a full refund.
  • Invoices checked for intra-state and inter-state orders.
  • Core Web Vitals and PageSpeed tested on category and product pages, which carry the most images.
  • Card data never touches your server; payments are handled on the gateway's side. Admin accounts get strong passwords and two-factor login where the platform supports it.
  • Automated backups of the product and order database, with a tested restore.

Mistakes that quietly cost sales

The ones we see most: forcing account creation before checkout, hiding shipping charges until the last step, no pincode check so buyers in outer sectors are unsure you deliver, unlimited COD with no confirmation step, and product pages with one blurry photo and no size or material details.

When you should not build your own store yet

If you sell only a handful of products and have no budget for ads or content, your own store will get little traffic at first. A marketplace such as Amazon or Flipkart, or a WhatsApp Business catalogue, may be a better first step. We will say so if that is the case. An own store makes sense once you want your own customer data, repeat orders and margins free of marketplace commissions.

What affects the quote

Cost depends on the platform, the number of products and variants, custom design versus a customised theme, integrations (ERP, billing software, CRM), B2B features and whether we handle product data entry and photography coordination. You get a fixed quote after a free consultation, with ongoing costs such as platform, app and gateway fees listed separately so there are no surprises.

Frequently asked questions

Should I sell on Amazon instead of building my own store?

Many brands do both. Marketplaces bring ready traffic but keep the customer relationship and take a commission. Your own store costs more to drive traffic to but lets you build repeat buyers. We can help you plan the order in which to do them.

Can I offer COD only in some areas?

Yes. COD can be limited by pincode, order value or product, and we can add an OTP or WhatsApp confirmation for COD orders before they are shipped.

Will the store produce GST invoices automatically?

Yes. Invoices are generated with your GSTIN, HSN codes and the right tax split for the delivery state. Your accountant should review the set-up once before launch.

Who owns the customer and order data?

You do. The store, gateway and shipping accounts are all opened in your company's name, and you can export customers and orders at any time.

Can you connect the store to our billing software?

Often, yes, depending on whether the software offers an API or import tools. We check this in the consultation before promising anything.
